Back two: Mega Blaziken (CC OHKOs Incineroar/Meowscarada, Flare Blitz OHKOs Metagross in sun) plus Gengar, the Fake-Out-immune special answer to Hatterene and Incineroar that ignores Inti
decisions.notebook: Series leads 1-0; game 2 team: Hippo+Excadrill lead, Mega Blaziken + Gengar back. Ironwood: Intimidate-cycle Incineroar, Drought Torkoal, Mega Metagross (confirmed all-Steel: Meteor Mash/Bullet Punch/Iron Head/Protect), TR Hatterene (Magic Bounce — NEVER Yawn it), Meowscarada, Mamoswine. Game 1 they benched Hatterene+Mamoswine; expect either/both as anti-sand adaptation. Torkoal (36-64) slower than Hippo (67): Drought overrides Sand on simultaneous lead; they open Fake Out + Eruption into Excadrill slot even vs Protect. Key calcs: Excadrill LO Iron Head OHKOs Hatterene guaranteed; Gengar Shadow Ball vs Hatterene 66-123% (not guaranteed through Sitrus) but Gengar is Fake-Out-immune; sun Eruption vs Gengar 68-132% — never lead Gengar into possible Torkoal; Gyarados Waterfall only 25-45% vs Torkoal in sun (not a real answer). Excadrill 220 sand-speed outspeeds max Meowscarada(192)/Mamoswine; LO EQ vs Mega Metagross 60-103%; resists entire all-Steel set. Mega Blaziken CC OHKOs Incineroar & Meowscarada guaranteed; CC KOs Torkoal from 41%; Flare Blitz vs Mega Metagross 84-143% (OHKO in sun). Meowscarada Play Rough KOs Blaziken from 53% — never expose Blaziken; sleep or KO Metagross before committing Blaziken (even resisted Mash KOs chipped Blaziken; +1 Mash KOs Hippo from ~54%, so Yawn Metagross freely — no switch = guaranteed sleep). Torkoal EP at -1 SpD KOs Blaziken from ~53%; sun Eruption OHKOs Excadrill. Passimian Defiant punishes Intimidate but Payapa is useless vs all-Steel Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Lead Incineroar/Torkoar to counter sand immediately. Incineroar Fake Out disrupts Hippowdon Yawn/Protect while Intimidate weakens Excadrill. Torkoal's Drought overrides sand, enabling full-power Eruption spread damage. Back Metagross (intended Mega) provides Steel-type offensive pressure and Tough Claws Meteor Mash after Mega. Meowscarada offers speed control and Grass coverage vs Water/Ground threats. This lead directly targets the opponent's primary sand strategy while preserving Mega Metagros
decisions.notebook: Opponent consistently leads Hippowdon/Excadrill sand; counter with Drought override and Fake Out disruption. Passimian Payapa Berry + Defiant punishes Intimidate - avoid dropping its Attack. Mega Blaziken Speed Boost requires immediate pressure or Taunt. Gyarados Intimidate + Sitrus indicates physical bulk preference. Gengar Colbur Berry suggests special attacker targeting Dark types. Future games: bring Taunt/Encore users to block Yawn and Speed Boost setup. Ground-immune pivots essential vs Excadrill sand. Target Hippowdon early to prevent sand/Yawn stall chains. Avoid Mega Metagross vs Hippowdon due to 4x Ground weakness and sleep vulnerability from Yawn.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill dies to sun Eruption, so Protect vs the telegraphed Fake Out + Eruption open. Hippowdon (67) outspeeds Torkoal (36-64): EQ hits both foes super-effectively (21-43% Torkoal, 24-53% Incineroar) before Eruption fires, dropping its BP, and Hippo tanks even full-power sun Eruption (32-69%). Turn 2 Excadrill is free to Rock Slide/Iron Head with both foes chipped.

This is the safest line: we avoid all damage this turn, maintain sun advantage, and preserve Torkoal's HP for Eruption next turn. Alternative lines risk Torkoal being KOed or severely damaged by Excadrill's Life Orb EQ.

reflections.summary: Lost due to a fundamentally mismatched team preview: bringing a slow Drought setter (Torkoal) and two Rock-weak/frail attackers (Incineroar, Meowscarada) against a Smooth Rock Hippowdon + Speed Boost Blaziken core guaranteed weather loss and Rock Slide vulnerability. Mega Metagross lacked speed control and was neutralized by sleep on entry, forcing Torkoal into a Protect stall that eventually failed against +6 Speed Blaziken.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Torkoal with a faster Rock-resistant Pokémon (e.g., Landorus-T, Gyarados, or a Water-type) that can immediately pressure Hippowdon and check Blaziken. Prioritize removing Hippowdon on turn 1 to prevent sand extension, and bring dedicated Speed control or priority to handle +6 Speed Blaziken without relying on Protect chains.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s win condition is Hippowdon (Smooth Rock) extending sand to enable Mega Blaziken’s Speed Boost sweep. Hippowdon heavily spams Rock Slide; critical hits and sleep support consistently enable setup. Blaziken remains lethal at +6 Speed even with multiple stat drops; must be KO’d or forced to Protect before acting. Drought is easily overridden by Smooth Rock sand; slow weather setters are ineffective. Future games require a Rock resist/immune and faster Speed control to break the sand setup. Gyarados, Passimian, and Gengar sets remain untested but likely support the core.
